experiments.title: Resume GRPO and save compact state
experiments.intent: Restore step 1, complete one additional Muon update, and save only adapter and training state without losing resumability.
experiments.change: Preload the pinned base before LoRA restore; exclude frozen base weights from new checkpoints. Keep the old checkpoint unchanged.
experiments.conclusion: Distributed restore from the original full checkpoint and optimizer step 2 passed. The new 68 MB checkpoint passed CPU read-back. This does not establish better kernel generation.
experiments.decision: Validate a distributed restart from the compact checkpoint before a longer run. Keep rank 8 and current hardware limits.
limitations: No distributed restart from the newly compact checkpoint yet.
One admitted cummax group is not a held-out quality comparison.
Recovery turns and child delegation were not exercised.

relationships.label: Retry after checkpoint key fix; not a trained-checkpoint dependency

experiments.title: First saved GRPO update
experiments.intent: Verify the real model can produce rollouts, supply a nonzero GRPO signal, update attention LoRA, and save training state.
experiments.change: Three A100s: one for inference/verifier access and two for expert-parallel training. Rank-8 attention LoRA with Muon.
experiments.conclusion: Step 1 and checkpoint read-back passed. Rewards [0, 0.1, 0, 0.1] supplied submission signal only; no admitted final kernel was correct.
experiments.decision: Use the saved state to validate resume and improve submission reliability before scaling training.
limitations: Three of five saved episodes reached the turn limit.
The original full checkpoint is about 134 GB; preserve it until compact resume is validated.

experiments.title: Give complete CUDA replies more room
experiments.intent: Reduce per-call truncations without expanding the context window or recovery budget.
experiments.change: Normal training reply cap: 2,048 → 4,096. Context remains 12,288; recovery 512; child output 2,048; four rollouts in flight.
experiments.conclusion: 40 focused CPU checks passed. No live model run has tested the larger reply cap.
experiments.decision: Use a bounded validation before a longer training launch; inspect output lengths, context pressure and GPU memory.
limitations: Longer replies may increase latency and context consumption.
No GPU memory or quality result at the new limit.

experiments.title: Make focused delegation easier
experiments.intent: Help the root delegate difficult kernel subproblems without requiring or rewarding unnecessary child calls.
experiments.change: Optional semantics, indexing, algorithm and compiler reviews; a small executable llm_query example stores advice and prints a short slice.
experiments.conclusion: 11 CPU checks passed, including the example through the real worker/proxy with a mocked child. No live delegation benefit is measured.
experiments.decision: Inspect optional child use on harder kernels. Judge correctness, tokens and time, not the number of child calls.
limitations: Children return untested text/code advice; they have no REPL or verifier.
No live comparison for this prompt yet.
